text:
I’m a passionate and hard-working developer with 7 years of experience building and maintaining web applications, and I’d love to help the Connecticut River Conservancy with your WordPress content management, maintenance, and troubleshooting needs.

My background is strongest in full stack JavaScript and front-end work, including JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. While my recent work has centered on modern web stacks, the same problem-solving approach applies directly to WordPress environments: improving performance, resolving broken functionality, streamlining workflows, and making systems easier for non-technical teams to use.

For Juniper & Ash Home, I rebuilt a slow theme-based shop into a headless storefront and CMS that the marketing team could edit themselves. That project reduced the largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.3s and improved organic traffic by 38% in 3 months. For Alder Property Group, I built a queue that renders owner statements to PDF overnight and stores them in S3 instead of generating them on demand, which handled 12k statements a month and took request timeouts from daily to none. Both projects reinforced how important stability, maintainability, and thoughtful optimization are in production systems.

For CRC, I would approach the work by first resolving the lingering issues around notifications, the event calendar, and default settings, then reviewing the current setup for maintenance, plugin health, and opportunities to simplify. I’m comfortable working closely with staff to support content and design collaboration, and I can help assess page-building strategy, front-end usability, hosting-related concerns, and data integration points. I also understand the value of clear troubleshooting and steady monthly maintenance so the site stays reliable over time.

I’d be glad to help you evaluate the current WordPress setup and improve it in a way that supports your team’s ongoing work.

What are the top three issues you want resolved first: notifications, event calendar behavior, or default settings?
